SVB.time_local: 2023-03-08, after US market close (SEC listing stamp ~17:26 ET = ~14:26 PT; exact release time unconfirmed, almost certainly before 17:00 PT)
SVB.text: SVB Financial announced sale of ~$21B AFS securities (~$1.8B after-tax loss), a mid-quarter update and investor letter, and a proposed $1.25B common + $500M mandatory convertible preferred offering, plus $500M General Atlantic private placement ($2.25B total). Said it was acting to strengthen balance sheet.
SVB.channel: Public press release / 8-K (Ex. 99.1-99.3) and investor letter
SVB.note: The General Atlantic commitment was conditional on the offering, so it never became a completed backstop; offering reported failed on Mar 9-10 (media/Goldman, sources).

SVB.time_local: 2023-03-09, Thursday afternoon (exact start not published; ~10-minute call)
SVB.text: CEO Greg Becker told top VC/clients on a call to stay calm and not panic, that SVB had ample liquidity except if everyone tells each other SVB is in trouble, and asked clients to support SVB as it had supported them. Could not promise the raise was the last.
SVB.channel: Client/VC conference call (quotes reported secondhand by Bloomberg, CNBC, The Information)
SVB.note: Verbatim quotes are from call participants, not an official transcript.

SVB.text: Relationship managers emailed some clients saying it was business as usual and offering to make themselves available for concerns.
Federal Reserve notified FDIC of deposit run, funding shortfall and likely inadequate liquidity; FDIC contacted California DFPI and began overnight resolution planning. Not public at the time.
SVB.channel: Non-public regulator-to-regulator communication (disclosed later in FDIC testimony)
SVB.note: Not a public reassurance; included for context only.

SVB.text: SIVB shares halted by NYSE pending news after falling another ~60% premarket; never reopened. (Exchange action, not a company statement. No company press release found for Mar 9 evening or Mar 10 morning.)

SVB.time_local: 2023-03-10 morning; FDIC testimony says 11:15 a.m. EST (clock basis ambiguous); AP said announced shortly before noon ET (~09:00 PT)
SVB.text: California DFPI took possession of Silicon Valley Bank citing inadequate liquidity and insolvency, and appointed the FDIC as receiver.
SVB.note: Time conflict between sources; treat as roughly 08:15-09:30 PT, announcement public by ~09:00 PT.

SVB.time_local: 2023-03-10 (time of day not on release; issued same day as closure, mid-day ET to afternoon)
SVB.text: FDIC created the Deposit Insurance National Bank of Santa Clara, moved insured deposits there, promised insured depositors access by Monday Mar 13, and said uninsured depositors would get an advance dividend plus receivership certificates. Branches to reopen Mar 13.
FDIC ran a weekend sale process, getting only two bidders and one valid offer on part of the bank; recoveries were judged too low.

SVB.time_local: 2023-03-12, Sunday evening (~18:00 ET, from memory; not verified here)
SVB.text: Treasury, Fed and FDIC joint statement: systemic risk exception so all SVB depositors fully protected; Fed to create Bank Term Funding Program.
SVB.note: After window end (Sat Mar 11 17:00 PT). Included only for context.

CS.text: CEO Ulrich Koerner told staff Credit Suisse has a strong capital base and liquidity, and not to conflate share price moves with the bank's capital position. A spokesperson confirmed the memo.
CS.channel: Internal memo leaked to Reuters, then widely reported

CS.time_local: 2022-10-01 to 10-02 (Sat-Sun; FT report published Sunday Oct 2 evening, exact time not found)
CS.text: Executives spent the weekend calling top clients, counterparties and investors to reassure on liquidity and capital; a CS executive told the FT they were receiving messages of support. A spokesman declined to comment on the FT report itself.
CS.channel: Private calls to clients/counterparties, reported by FT/Reuters; executive quoted anonymously
CS.note: Individual caller names not found in sources reviewed. Anonymous executive quote, so semi-official.

CS.time_local: 2022-10-03 (Monday, during Zurich trading; exact time not found)
CS.text: A CS executive said the bank had not formally approached investors about new capital; reports (Reuters/Proactive) conflict on whether talks with investors existed.
CS circulated talking points to executives handling clients who asked about the CDS spike, stressing strong capital and liquidity, per Bloomberg.
CS.channel: Internal talking points leaked to Bloomberg

CS.text: No public FINMA or SNB statement on Credit Suisse found in the window; the joint FINMA/SNB statements came in March 2023. FINMA reportedly stepped up crisis-management work in early October, not public.
CS.note: Absence-of-evidence entry; no backstop or closure occurred in window.
